Follow the outline below, but adapt as needed — add sections if relevant, and omit those that do not apply to this project.

- Title the document "Repository Guidelines".
- Use Markdown headings (#, ##, etc.) for structure.
- Keep the document concise. 200-400 words is optimal.
- Keep explanations short, direct, and specific to this repository.
- Provide examples where helpful (commands, directory paths, naming patterns).
- Maintain a professional, instructional tone.

Project Structure & Module Organization

Build, Test, and Development Commands

Testing Guidelines

- State test naming conventions and how to run tests.

Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Summarize commit message conventions found in the project’s Git history.
- Outline pull request requirements (descriptions, linked issues, screenshots, etc.).

(Optional) Add other sections if relevant, such as Security & Configuration Tips, Architecture Overview, or Agent-Specific Instructions.

{"command":["bash","-lc","cat <<'EOF' > AGENTS.md
# Repository Guidelines

## Project Structure & Module Organization
- `PcShare/` hosts the MFC GUI that operators use; `res/` holds icons and dialogs, and `PcShare.rc` maps every resource ID.
- `PcMain/` contains low-level transports (LZW compression, socket wrappers, upload/download flows) that the GUI and services reuse.
- `PcMake/` bundles service utilities and shared helpers (`MyFunc`, `MyClientTran`, etc.) used to compose deployment payloads; `hlp/` and `res/` keep auxiliary assets.
- `PcStart/` is the lightweight launcher/bootstrapper that initializes common code before handing control to `PcShare.exe`.
- `bin/` stores packaged artifacts (`PcShare.exe`, `PcShare.ini`, geo DB `QQWry.dat`); treat it as runtime output, not a source directory.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands
- `devenv PcShare/PcShare.dsw /build "Release|Win32"` compiles the operator GUI and drops binaries in `PcShare/Release/`.
- `devenv PcMake/PcMake.dsw /build "Release|Win32"` rebuilds the service utilities; repeat for `PcMain` and `PcStart` as needed.
- `devenv <path>.dsw /build "Debug|Win32"` gives a symbol-rich debug build—use when investigating transport bugs.
- Manual smoke test: `bin/PcShare.exe` with `PcShare.ini` pointing at a local loopback listener validates startup without contacting production endpoints.

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
- Follow the established MFC pattern: classes prefixed with `C` or `My`, PascalCase for types, camelCase for locals, and uppercase macros/constants.
- Files use tabs that render as four spaces, braces on a new line for functions, and Win32/MFC typedefs (`DWORD`, `LPCTSTR`).
- Shared headers such as `MyMacro.h`, `StdAfx.h`, and resource headers must remain ASCII; guard new includes behind `#ifdef _DEBUG` when debug-only.
- Prefer existing helpers (e.g., `MySocket`, `MyFunc`) before introducing third-party code; keep string handling ANSI-compatible unless you extend Unicode handling across all modules.

## Testing Guidelines
- No automated suite exists; add focused harnesses in the relevant project (e.g., temporary dialog in `PcShare`) and remove before commit.
- Name exploratory tests `Test_<Scenario>` and document expected output inline.
- Before pushing, exercise file transfers (upload/download queues), socks proxy startup, and telnet modules using a disposable environment; confirm logs write to `bin/CACHE` only.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
- The imported snapshot lacks prior Git history, so use imperative, 72-character subject lines prefixed with the touched module (`PcShare: fix socket retry`).
- Describe observable behavior changes, note which `.dsw` projects to rebuild, and link tracking IDs or tickets.
- Pull requests should include: summary, risk assessment, manual test notes (commands/output), and screenshots for any UI adjustments.

## Security & Configuration Tips
- Keep secrets out of the repo; reference them via `PcShare.ini` keys and store actual values in a secure share.
- `QQWry.dat` is large and rarely modified—do not rewrite it unless updating the IP database, and document the source in your PR.
- When touching networking code, call out firewall/AV exceptions needed for QA so operators can reproduce without disabling protections.
EOF"],"workdir":"C:\Users\Jeff\Documents\GitHub\PcFileMan"}

## Project Structure & Module Organization
- PcShare/ hosts the MFC GUI operators use; res/ stores icons and dialogs while PcShare.rc maps resource identifiers.
- PcMain/ contains low level transports such as LZW compression, socket wrappers, and upload or download tasks reused by every module.
- PcMake/ bundles service utilities plus shared helpers like MyFunc and MyClientTran for building deployment payloads; hlp/ and res/ keep supporting assets.
- PcStart/ is the lightweight launcher that initializes shared code before starting PcShare.exe in the field.
- bin/ holds packaged artifacts (PcShare.exe, PcShare.ini, QQWry.dat); treat it as runtime output rather than editable source.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands
- Use a Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt and run devenv PcShare/PcShare.dsw /build "Release|Win32" to produce the operator GUI in PcShare/Release/.
- Run devenv PcMake/PcMake.dsw /build "Release|Win32" to refresh the service utilities; repeat for PcMain and PcStart whenever you touch shared transport code.
- Build debug variants with devenv <path>.dsw /build "Debug|Win32" when diagnosing socket or compression defects.
- Manual smoke test: launch bin/PcShare.exe with PcShare.ini pointing to a loopback listener to confirm startup without contacting production servers.

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
- Follow the existing MFC conventions: prefix classes with C or My, use PascalCase for types, camelCase for locals, and uppercase macros or resource identifiers.
- Source files are tab indented (tabs display as four spaces) and place braces on their own line for functions and control blocks.
- Prefer Win32 types such as DWORD or LPCTSTR and reuse helper layers (MySocket, MyFunc) before adding third party code; guard debug helpers with #ifdef _DEBUG.
- Keep shared headers (StdAfx.h, MyMarco.h, Resource.h) ASCII only and update include order consistently across projects.

## Testing Guidelines
- No automated harness exists; create temporary view or dialog hooks in the relevant project for new logic and remove them before committing.
- Name exploratory utilities TestScenario_<Name> and document assertions inline so reviewers understand expectations.
